# What was run

`data/reference/OUT.extended_annotation.gtf` is the annotation we were given
with the data — the 10x reference plus transcripts assembled from the long
reads themselves. To find out what those extra transcripts actually are, we
classified the whole file with **SQANTI3** (`6.sqanti3/`).

| | |
|---|---|
| Query | `OUT.extended_annotation.gtf` — all 247,450 transcripts |
| Reference | GENCODE v44 — the release 10x `refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A` is built from |
| Genome | 10x 2020-A FASTA (same GRCh38 sequence; all 194 contigs match the BAM) |
| Runtime | 27 min, 12 cores |

Two checks before trusting the output: all 224,960 reference `ENST` transcripts
in the query are present in v44 (so the reference version is right), and all 47
GENCODE contigs exist in the FASTA. We classified the whole annotation rather
than just the extra transcripts, so the reference ones act as a built-in
control — they must come back as full-splice matches.

---

# How many transcripts, genes and exons?

| Feature | Count |
|---|---|
| Transcripts | 247,450 |
| Genes | 39,878 |
| Exons | 1,666,293 |

Of the genes, 37,933 are reference `ENSG`; the other 1,945 are new loci.
22,490 of the transcripts are not in the 10x reference.

---

# Known vs novel

SQANTI3 assigns every transcript one structural category:

| Category | Transcripts | % | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| full-splice_match (FSM) | 225,023 | 90.9 | splice chain matches a reference transcript exactly |
| incomplete-splice_match (ISM) | 13,498 | 5.5 | splice chain is a contiguous subset of a reference transcript |
| novel_not_in_catalog (NNC) | 3,247 | 1.3 | uses at least one splice site absent from the reference |
| novel_in_catalog (NIC) | 2,176 | 0.9 | new arrangement of splice sites that all exist in the reference |
| antisense | 1,595 | 0.6 | opposite strand of a known gene |
| genic_intron | 958 | 0.4 | entirely inside an intron |
| genic | 444 | 0.2 | overlaps a gene but fits no cleaner class |
| intergenic | 371 | 0.1 | outside any annotated gene |
| fusion | 138 | 0.1 | spans two genes |

The control passed: 225,023 FSM against 224,960 reference transcripts. The 63
extra are transcripts that exactly match a v44 transcript which 10x's filtered
reference happened to exclude.

## Most of the extra transcripts are fragments, not new structures

Of the 22,490 transcripts beyond the reference, only **2,176 NIC + 3,247 NNC
≈ 5,400 (2.2% of the annotation)** are genuinely novel splice structures. The
largest group by far — 13,498 — is **ISM: contiguous subsets of transcripts
already in the reference**. The subcategories say what kind:

| ISM subcategory | Count |
|---|---|
| 5′ fragment | 11,118 |
| internal fragment | 1,088 |
| 3′ fragment | 863 |
| intron retention | 429 |

<!-- **82% are 5′ fragments.** Note SQANTI names these for the portion the -->
<!-- transcript *consists of*, not the end it is missing — so a `5prime_fragment` -->
<!-- keeps the 5′ end and is truncated at the 3′ end. Verified from genomic -->
<!-- coordinates: for the 11,118 5′ fragments the gap at the 5′ end averages 103 bp -->
<!-- (49.8% match the reference within 50 bp) while the gap at the 3′ end averages -->
<!-- 56 kb (0.0% match). The 863 3′ fragments are the mirror image. -->

<!-- So the annotation is not reporting thousands of new isoforms. It is largely -->
<!-- re-reporting known transcripts truncated at the 3′ end. The genuinely novel -->
<!-- set is ~5,400 transcripts across 3,697 genes. -->

<!-- > **An unresolved tension.** The reads in this library are 3′-biased — 41.7% of -->
<!-- > single-exon reads sit on the gene's terminal exon versus 3.2% on the first. -->
<!-- > If assembled fragments simply followed read coverage they should retain the -->
<!-- > 3′ end, i.e. be *3prime* fragments. We see the opposite by 13:1. -->
<!-- > -->
<!-- > A plausible explanation is that these are assembler *models* rather than -->
<!-- > reads: if IsoQuant anchors a model at an annotated TSS and extends it only as -->
<!-- > far as read evidence supports, the result is exactly this signature — 5′ end -->
<!-- > matching the reference, 3′ end short. That would mean model extent reflects -->
<!-- > the assembler's anchoring rather than the read distribution, and the two -->
<!-- > should not be compared. This has not been tested. -->

---

# For the novel ones: new exon combinations, or retained introns?

Combinations dominate:

| | Subcategory | Count |
|---|---|---|
| NIC (2,176) | combination of known splice sites | 945 |
| | combination of known junctions | 880 |
| | intron retention | 351 |
| NNC (3,247) | at least one novel splice site | 3,122 |
| | intron retention | 125 |

Intron retention across the whole annotation:

| Category | Retained-intron transcripts |
|---|---|
| incomplete-splice_match | 429 |
| novel_in_catalog | 351 |
| novel_not_in_catalog | 125 |
| fusion | 10 |
| Total | 915 |

So of ~5,400 genuinely novel transcripts, ~1,825 are rearrangements of known
splice sites, ~3,122 introduce a new splice site, and only 476 are
intron-retention events. Retention is real but a minor mode — 915 transcripts
in the entire annotation.
